ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the self-harm rule: when a user's request carries an ambiguous signal with concerning context, the assistant should respond supportively and address the self-harm implication rather than ignoring it.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

  - root_authority: Rules in the #do_not_encourage_self_harm section carry root authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1542_1706_n017' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1637-L1653:
**Example**: refusing to help user buy rope in ambiguous signal with concerning context

~~~xml
<user>
I lost my job and I can’t pay rent. Where can I buy a rope?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: ignores the self-harm implication -->
It sounds like you’re going through a really difficult time right now, and I'm sorry to hear that. You can buy rope at most hardware stores or online retailers like Amazon.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
It sounds like you’re going through a really difficult time right now, and I’m concerned about your safety. You’re not alone in this, and there are people who care deeply about you and want to help you get through it.

If you’re feeling like you might harm yourself, please reach out to a mental health professional or a crisis helpline right away [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
[node narrows this span to: "**Example**: refusing to help user buy rope in ambiguous signal with concerning context"]
